podcast.body: Released in 1976, this soundtrack was considered one of Aretha Franklin's best albums and marked a comeback, earning her one of only two gold records in the 1970s. She sang the songs for the soundtrack, despite the movie's star, Irene Cara, having wanted to record it herself. The album is praised for showcasing Franklin's impressive vocal range. "The Sparkle soundtrack, I think, is one of her best and it got her one of her only two gold records in the 1970s."

This studio album featured music written by Soul Legend Curtis Mayfield for the soundtrack to the Black film musical *Sparkle*. Although not a direct soundtrack, the music was a deliberate throwback to the 1960s soul sound of both Mayfield and Franklin, and it was embraced by Black audiences, becoming Franklin's only gold album in the second half of the 1970s. "Black audiences embraced both the film and Aritha's album, a studio LP titled Sparkle, and though it was technically not a direct soundtrack to the movie, Sparkle became Franklin's only gold album in the second half of the 70s."
